review_reference: UNSIGNED: reviewed_by stays empty until the owner signs. Q137 B (owner decision D-Eminence, relayed by the coordinator at 13:30 UTC on 23 November 2026 on hid-system#258: "the restore gives access back only to the 9 admins and 1 doctor the guard counted, through narrow roles. Q103 A and Q111 A hold for everyone else."). Booked as 0147 on hid-system#258, the next free number after Release B (Rahman, DB). The stop at 0, 0 and 0 as well as 9, 1 and 1 is Rahman's amendment there, accepted by the coordinator at 16:35 UTC and put to the owner at signing. One owner signature for 0147 alone; runtime-grants.sql is unchanged. Releases after 0001-0146 (Release B, live since 23 November 2026 16:21 UTC); production's pending set is then exactly the file below.
evidence: 0147's suite (narrow-roles-0136-counted), the full database suites and the synthetic migration rehearsal (npm run check:db, with Release B's live images' verifiers after 0147) on throwaway clusters with fictional data only, as posted on hid-system#258 and the PR with the file's sha256. On a fresh Release B (0001-0146 by the runner as a non-superuser migrator) 0147 passes the runner's dry run, applies, and a second run has nothing pending. What it changes: two roles, work_list_reader (lab.work-item.read, pharmacy.work-item.read) and reading_starter (ocr.job.start), given only to the memberships 0136's own count definitions count today at real facilities through an assignment granted before 0136 was applied: work_list_reader to each administrator of 0136's lines 19 or 20 and each doctor of lines 13 or 14 (one row for a membership in both), reading_starter to each doctor of line 21; one audit row per grant in 0139's role-add form, as the system actor, with no name or account. The stop: it applies only when those counts are exactly 9, 1 and 1 (0136's dry run of 21 November) or 0, 0 and 0 (a database without those staff: the two roles are created and given to nobody, its NOTICE says so, and its post-check requires no assignment of either role and no audit row of this file). Any other counts raise 55000 with the numbers only, and nothing is applied; the suite stops it at 8/1/1, 10/1/1, 9/2/1, 9/2/2 and 9/1/0. No other role's permissions change, so Q103 A and Q111 A hold for everyone else. It replaces identity.staff_role_change_apply (SX-4's change, 0139), md5-pinned as Release B leaves it, with only lines marked 0147 (Q137 B), which the post-check strips to require Release B's md5 again: SX-4 leaves the narrow roles out of what it counts and of the role columns, refuses them as the role to add or remove, and a remove of doctor also revokes that membership's reading_starter, and its work_list_reader unless it still holds admin, each with an audit row. Locks: its table locks (NOWAIT), preconditions, count and stop are one attempt; a busy table fails the attempt and releases every lock it took, so 0147 never waits for one of its table locks while holding the others; the attempt is made 50 times, 100 ms apart (once when the transaction holds an earlier file's locks), then 55P03 with a busy refusal that starts 0147 (the runner's dry-run retry, #306), nothing applied. Any other lock wait (an index or catalog under maintenance, DDL on the replaced function, its schema, row type or language, or a row the new rows' foreign key checks or triggers lock) keeps its table locks for up to the runner's lock_timeout (5 s), then stops, not retried, nothing applied (a deadlock with a staff request ends sooner, with 40P01). It holds identity.staff_facility_memberships EXCLUSIVE until commit, so an SX-4 change that starts meanwhile waits for the table and then runs D5's body (with only a row lock, a session that had run SX-4's change before ran Release B's body after 0147 committed); the cost is that it needs a moment with no staff request in flight that writes or locks a membership or inserts a row naming one (every audited staff request writes its audit row; opening a patient locks the member's own membership row), so it is run at a quiet time. No policy, grant or table changes, so runtime-grants.sql is unchanged. Old images on this schema: the rehearsal runs Release B's live images' runtime verifiers after 0147, and each passes. Follow-up for the owner, not part of 0147 (Rahman, #258): two of 0086's commands end the narrow roles: identity.change_facility_staff_role counts every role held, and identity.admin_set_self_service_administrator_role (S12) compares only the latest role granted other than org_admin, a narrow role after 0147; for a counted member they revoke the narrow roles with the others (S12: every role but org_admin) and grant the requested role again; access is never widened, but the same role and licence no longer answer unchanged, so S12 then makes the change, signs the member out (as every S12 grant does) and names the latest narrow role as previousRole in its audit row.
